claim: RouterDC trains a query-based router with dual contrastive learning to select the single most suitable off-the-shelf LLM per query, outperforming individual top-performing LLMs and prior routing methods.
scope_conditions: in-distribution and out-of-distribution query benchmarks, NeurIPS 2024, whole-query granularity
quoted_support: Experimental results show that RouterDC is effective in assembling LLMs and largely outperforms individual top-performing LLMs as well as existing routing methods on both in-distribution (+2.76%) and out-of-distribution (+1.90%) tasks.

claim: Existing routing models are ineffective when multiple LLMs perform comparably well on a query, motivating dual contrastive learning to sharpen router discrimination.
quoted_support: existing routing models are ineffective when multiple LLMs perform well for a query.

claim: RouterDC assigns exactly one LLM per whole query with no mechanism to compose or route different sub-tasks/requirements of the same query to different models.
stance_target: novelty of per-requirement cross-model routing (candidate c)
quoted_support: Recent works show that assembling multiple off-the-shelf large language models (LLMs) can harness their complementary abilities. To achieve this, routing is a promising method, which learns a router to select the most suitable LLM for each query.
